key_insight: LATHE turns natural-language design hypotheses into differentiable geometric edits on crystal structures, enabling fine-grained control over seven crystallographic properties without generating structures from scratch.
engineering_relevance: The toolkit provides a practical closed-loop workflow for materials design, letting engineers directly enforce symmetry and geometry constraints while preserving proximity to low-energy, physically plausible structures.
method: Defines seven crystal properties as differentiable objectives: bond length, bond angle, dihedral angle, coordination environment, lattice parameters, cell volume, and space group.
Uses gradient-based editing to modify an existing crystal structure under user-specified constraints.
Exposes the toolkit through an MCP server and a multi-agent loop that translates natural-language hypotheses into executable geometric operations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports near-perfect satisfaction across all seven benchmarked property types, >87.5% valid execution of natural-language prompts, and 9/10 success in a band-gap inverse-design case study within about 13 hypothesis-evaluation cycles.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurate objective definitions and optimization stability, and the natural-language agent still needs robust validation to avoid invalid or mis-specified editing commands.
paper_title: LATHE: LAnguage-driven Toolkit for Hypothesis-based crystal Editing
